title: Single Neuron Weighted Sum
plainTextFormula: z = w^T x + b
description: Computes the pre-activation value of a single neuron from input features, weights, and bias.

shape.explanation: The dot product collapses the feature dimension into one scalar neuron signal.

title: Single Neuron Activation Output
plainTextFormula: a = g(z)
description: Applies a nonlinear activation to the pre-activation value so the neuron can model more than a linear mapping.

shape.explanation: Elementwise activations preserve the leading shape of their input.

title: Dense Layer Forward Pass
description: The default affine-activation block used by feed-forward neural network layers.

shape.explanation: Matrix multiplication maps the previous activation width to the current layer width across all examples.

title: Sigmoid Activation
plainTextFormula: sigma(z) = 1 / (1 + e^-z)
description: Maps a real-valued logit into the open interval between 0 and 1.

shape.explanation: Sigmoid is applied elementwise.

title: Sigmoid Derivative
plainTextFormula: sigma prime z = sigma z times one minus sigma z
description: Derivative used when backpropagating through sigmoid activations.

shape.explanation: Elementwise derivatives keep the same tensor shape.

title: ReLU Activation
plainTextFormula: ReLU(z) = max(0, z)
description: Keeps positive values and clips negative values to zero.

shape.explanation: ReLU is an elementwise hidden-layer nonlinearity.

title: Softmax Activation
plainTextFormula: softmax(z)_k = exp(z_k) / sum_j exp(z_j)
description: Turns class logits into a probability distribution over K classes.

shape.output: softmax(z): same class shape as z
shape.explanation: Softmax normalizes across the class dimension.

title: Binary Cross-Entropy Loss
plainTextFormula: L(a,y) = -[y log a + (1-y) log(1-a)]
description: Penalizes confident wrong predictions in binary classification.

shape.explanation: A single example loss is a scalar; batch cost averages these scalars.

title: Categorical Cross-Entropy Loss
plainTextFormula: L(yhat,y) = - sum_k y_k log yhat_k
description: Measures mismatch between a predicted class distribution and a one-hot target.

shape.explanation: The sum collapses K class terms into one loss value.

title: Mean Squared Error
plainTextFormula: J = 1/m sum_i 1/2 ||yhat_i - y_i||^2
description: A smooth regression objective that squares prediction error.

shape.explanation: Errors are squared and averaged over the mini-batch.

title: Dense Layer dZ
plainTextFormula: dZ[l] = dA[l] * g'[l](Z[l])
description: Converts activation gradient into pre-activation gradient for one dense layer.

symbols.meaning: Gradient of the cost with respect to pre-activations

shape.explanation: Elementwise multiplication preserves layer activation shape.

title: Dense Layer Weight Gradient
plainTextFormula: dW[l] = 1/m dZ[l] (A[l-1])^T
description: Gradient of dense layer weights with respect to the loss.

symbols.meaning: Gradient of the loss with respect to weights

shape.explanation: The batch dimension cancels in the matrix product, leaving the same shape as W.

title: Dense Layer Bias Gradient
plainTextFormula: db[l] = 1/m sum_i dZ[l](i)
description: Averages pre-activation gradients across the batch to match the bias vector shape.

shape.explanation: Summing across examples removes the batch axis.

title: Dense Layer dA Previous
plainTextFormula: dA[l-1] = (W[l])^T dZ[l]
description: Propagates the gradient signal from one layer back to the previous layer's activations.

symbols.meaning: Gradient for the previous layer activations

shape.explanation: The current layer width cancels, recovering the previous activation shape.

title: Dense Layer Activation Shape
plainTextFormula: A[l], Z[l], dA[l], dZ[l] are n[l] x m
description: Core dense-layer batch shape used to check forward and backward propagation.

symbols.meaning: Number of units in layer l

shape.explanation: Rows represent units; columns represent batch examples.

title: Logistic Regression dZ Shortcut
plainTextFormula: dZ = A - Y
description: The sigmoid plus binary cross-entropy simplification for the output-layer logit gradient.

shape.explanation: Both operands share the output-layer batch shape.

title: Softmax Cross-Entropy dZ Shortcut
plainTextFormula: dZ = A - Y
description: The softmax plus categorical cross-entropy simplification for output-layer gradients.

shape.explanation: The class-by-batch shape stays unchanged.

title: Gradient Descent Update
plainTextFormula: theta <- theta - alpha dtheta
description: Generic first-order parameter update that moves against the gradient.

shape.explanation: Updates do not change parameter dimensions.

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent Update
plainTextFormula: theta_{t+1} = theta_t - eta g_t
description: Updates parameters using the current mini-batch gradient.

shape.explanation: Optimizer updates move values but preserve the parameter tensor shape.

title: Momentum Update Rule
plainTextFormula: v_t = beta v_{t-1} + (1-beta) g_t, theta_{t+1} = theta_t - eta v_t
description: Smooths noisy gradients by carrying a velocity-like moving average.

symbols.meaning: Velocity or moving average of gradients

shape.explanation: Momentum stores one accumulator per parameter.

title: RMSProp Update Rule
plainTextFormula: s_t = rho s_{t-1} + (1-rho)(g_t*g_t), theta = theta - eta g_t/(sqrt(s_t)+epsilon)
description: Scales updates by a moving average of squared gradients.

shape.explanation: RMSProp keeps one squared-gradient accumulator per parameter.

title: Adam Update Rule
plainTextFormula: Adam m_t beta1 momentum, v_t beta2 squared gradients, theta update with mhat over sqrt(vhat)
description: Combines momentum-like gradient averaging with RMSProp-style adaptive scaling.

shape.explanation: Adam keeps two accumulators with the same shape as each parameter.

title: Initialization Parameter Shapes
plainTextFormula: W[l] shape n[l] x n[l-1], b[l] shape n[l] x 1, fan_in = n[l-1], fan_out = n[l]
description: Defines the layer-wise weight, bias, fan-in, and fan-out shapes used by all initialization rules.

shape.explanation: Initialization samples one value for every trainable weight and bias entry.

title: Zero Initialization
description: A reference initialization that is safe for biases but causes a hidden-unit symmetry problem when all hidden-layer weight matrices start at zero.

shape.output: all parameter entries set to zero
shape.explanation: The tensor shapes are valid, but hidden-layer weights should not all share the same initial value.

title: Small Random Initialization
plainTextFormula: W[l] sampled from N(0, sigma^2), b[l] = 0
description: Samples small random weights to break hidden-unit symmetry while keeping biases at zero.

shape.explanation: Random sampling changes initial values while preserving the layer's parameter dimensions.

title: Xavier / Glorot Variance
plainTextFormula: Var(W[l]) = 2 / (fan_in + fan_out)
description: Chooses variance using both fan-in and fan-out to stabilize signal scale in tanh or sigmoid-style networks.

shape.explanation: The variance parameter controls the distribution used to sample the whole weight matrix.

title: Xavier Normal Initialization
plainTextFormula: W[l] sampled from N(0, 2/(fan_in + fan_out))
description: Samples weights from a normal distribution using the Glorot variance.

shape.explanation: Every weight entry is sampled independently with the Xavier variance.

title: Xavier Uniform Initialization
plainTextFormula: W[l] sampled from U(-sqrt(6/(fan_in+fan_out)), sqrt(6/(fan_in+fan_out)))
description: Samples weights from the uniform Xavier / Glorot interval.

shape.explanation: The interval is chosen so the sampled weights have the Xavier variance scale.

title: Course Simplified Xavier Variance
plainTextFormula: Var(W[l]) = 1 / fan_in
description: A simplified Xavier-style convention used in some course notes.

shape.explanation: The simplified rule depends only on the number of incoming units.

title: He Initialization Variance
plainTextFormula: Var(W[l]) = 2 / fan_in
description: Chooses variance using fan-in for ReLU-style hidden layers.

shape.explanation: The variance scale is larger than simplified Xavier to match ReLU-style activations.

title: He Normal Initialization
plainTextFormula: W[l] sampled from N(0, 2/fan_in)
description: Samples ReLU-style weights from a normal distribution with He variance.

shape.explanation: Every weight entry is sampled independently with He variance.

title: He Scaled Random Matrix
plainTextFormula: W[l] = sqrt(2/n[l-1]) R[l], R[l] sampled from N(0,1)
description: Writes He initialization as a scaled standard-normal random matrix.

symbols.meaning: Number of units in the previous layer

shape.explanation: The scalar scale factor changes variance but not matrix shape.

title: Bias Initialization
plainTextFormula: b[l] = 0, b[l] shape n[l] x 1
description: Initializes biases to zero; random weights already break hidden-unit symmetry.

shape.explanation: Bias initialization preserves the layer's bias-column shape.

title: L2 Regularized Cost
plainTextFormula: J_reg = J + lambda/(2m) sum_l ||W[l]||_F^2
description: Adds a weight-size penalty to discourage overly large parameters; bias terms are usually not included.

symbols.meaning: Squared Frobenius norm of layer weights

shape.explanation: All layer penalties are summed into one scalar cost.

title: L2 Regularized Weight Gradient
plainTextFormula: dW_reg[l] = dW[l] + lambda/m W[l]
description: Adds the derivative of the L2 weight penalty to the ordinary weight gradient.

shape.explanation: The penalty term has the same shape as dW, so the gradient shape is preserved.

title: L2 Weight Decay Update
plainTextFormula: W[l] <- W[l] - alpha (dW[l] + lambda/m W[l])
description: Applies the regularized gradient inside the weight update.

shape.explanation: The update changes values but preserves the weight matrix shape.

title: Equivalent L2 Shrinkage Form
plainTextFormula: W[l] <- (1 - alpha lambda/m) W[l] - alpha dW[l]
description: Shows L2 regularization as a multiplicative shrinkage of weights before the ordinary gradient step.

shape.explanation: The scalar shrinkage factor broadcasts over every weight entry.

title: Dropout Mask
plainTextFormula: D[l] sampled from Bernoulli(p_keep), D[l] shape n[l] x m
description: Samples which units survive dropout during training.

symbols.meaning: Probability that an activation is kept

shape.explanation: The mask has one keep/drop value per activation.

title: Inverted Dropout Forward Pass
plainTextFormula: A_tilde[l] = D[l] * A[l], A_drop[l] = D[l] * A[l] / p_keep
description: Scales surviving activations during training so inference needs no extra scaling.

shape.explanation: Elementwise masking and scaling preserve activation shape.

title: Dropout Training-Time Scaling
plainTextFormula: A[l] <- D[l] * A[l] / p_keep during training
description: Applies inverted dropout during training so the expected activation scale stays aligned with inference.

shape.explanation: The training rule changes activation values while preserving the activation matrix shape.

title: Dropout Inference Convention
plainTextFormula: A_test[l] = A[l]
description: Turns dropout off at validation and inference time when using inverted dropout scaling during training.

shape.explanation: Inference keeps the full activation matrix because train-time scaling already handled expected scale.

title: Early Stopping Rule
plainTextFormula: stop at t* = arg min_t J_dev(t)
description: Selects the training step with the best dev-set cost instead of continuing until training cost is smallest.

symbols.meaning: Dev-set cost at training step t

input: dev cost curve over training steps
shape.explanation: Early stopping is a selection rule over scalar dev-set costs, not a tensor operation.

title: Data Augmentation Transform
plainTextFormula: (x, y) maps to (T(x), y)
description: Creates a label-preserving transformed input so the model sees more valid variations of the same target.

shape.output: T(x) with the same label y
shape.explanation: The input can change, but the supervised target remains the same.

title: Bias-Variance Decomposition
plainTextFormula: Expected Error = Bias^2 + Variance + Noise
description: Conceptual decomposition used to reason about underfitting and overfitting.

symbols.meaning: Error from sensitivity to the training set

shape.explanation: This is a conceptual diagnostic formula, not a tensor operation.

title: Mini-batch Gradient Estimate
plainTextFormula: g_t = 1/B sum over mini-batch gradients
description: Estimates the gradient using only the current mini-batch.

shape.explanation: Averaging gradients preserves parameter shape.

title: CNN Tensor Convention (NHWC)
latex: A^{[l-1]}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_H^{[l-1]}\times n_W^{[l-1]}\times n_C^{[l-1]}},\quad A^{[l]}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_H^{[l]}\times n_W^{[l]}\times n_C^{[l]}}
plainTextFormula: A[l-1] shape m x nH[l-1] x nW[l-1] x nC[l-1], A[l] shape m x nH[l] x nW[l] x nC[l]
description: Sets the NHWC batch tensor convention used by the CNN formulas in this hub.

shape.explanation: CNN activations keep batch, height, width, and channel axes explicit.

title: CNN Output Size (1D/2D)
plainTextFormula: nH[l] = floor((nH[l-1] + 2p[l] - f[l]) / s[l]) + 1, nW[l] = floor((nW[l-1] + 2p[l] - f[l]) / s[l]) + 1, nC[l] = number of filters
description: Computes the height, width, and channel count after a convolution layer.

shape.explanation: Apply the same floor formula separately to height and width; channels equal the filter count.

title: Convolution Operation
plainTextFormula: Z[l](i)_{h,w,k} = sum_u sum_v sum_c A[l-1](i)_{h_u,w_v,c} W[l]_{u,v,c,k} + b[l]_k
description: Computes one output location and output channel by summing over a local spatial window and all input channels.

input: filter slice for k: same shape
shape.explanation: One filter produces one scalar at each output spatial location and channel.

title: Convolution Parameter Count
plainTextFormula: params per filter = f[l] f[l] nC[l-1] + 1, params layer = (f[l] f[l] nC[l-1] + 1) nC[l]
description: Counts weights and biases in a standard convolution layer.

shape.explanation: Each output channel owns a full input-channel filter plus one bias.

title: CNN Padding Conventions
plainTextFormula: valid padding p = 0, same padding with stride 1 p = (f - 1) / 2
description: Summarizes valid and same padding conventions for convolution output shapes.

shape.explanation: Same padding with stride 1 preserves spatial size when the padding value is an integer.

title: Pooling Output Size
plainTextFormula: pool nH[l] = floor((nH[l-1] - f) / s) + 1, nW[l] = floor((nW[l-1] - f) / s) + 1, nC[l] = nC[l-1]
description: Computes spatial size after pooling while preserving the number of channels.

shape.explanation: Pooling shrinks height and width but normally keeps channel count unchanged.

title: Max Pooling
plainTextFormula: A[l](i)_{h,w,c} = max over pooling window R_{h,w} A[l-1](i)_{u,v,c}
description: Keeps the strongest activation inside each pooling window.

symbols.meaning: Pooling window at output location h,w

shape.explanation: Pooling is applied independently to each channel.

title: Average Pooling
plainTextFormula: A[l](i)_{h,w,c} = average over pooling window R_{h,w} A[l-1](i)_{u,v,c}
description: Keeps the mean activation inside each pooling window.

symbols.meaning: Number of spatial positions in the pooling window

shape.explanation: Average pooling is channelwise just like max pooling.

title: 1x1 Convolution Channel Projection
latex: \#params=(1\cdot1\cdot n_C^{[l-1]}+1)n_C^{[l]},\quad A^{[l-1]}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_H\times n_W\times n_C^{[l-1]}}\rightarrow A^{[l]}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_H\times n_W\times n_C^{[l]}}
plainTextFormula: 1x1 conv params = (1*1*nC[l-1] + 1) nC[l], changes channels while keeping H and W
description: Uses a 1x1 filter to project channel width while keeping spatial height and width unchanged.

shape.explanation: A 1x1 convolution changes channel depth without changing spatial resolution.

title: Depthwise Separable Convolution Parameters
plainTextFormula: standard conv params = k^2 C_in C_out, depthwise separable params = k^2 C_in + C_in C_out
description: Compares standard convolution parameters with depthwise plus pointwise convolution parameters.

shape.explanation: Depthwise separable convolution replaces full channel mixing with depthwise spatial filters plus a 1x1 pointwise projection.

title: Feature Map Activation
plainTextFormula: Feature map k = phi(W_k * input + b_k)
description: Represents how strongly filter k responds across spatial positions.

shape.explanation: Each filter creates one output feature map channel.

title: Sequence Tensor Convention
plainTextFormula: a sequence is a list of time-step tensors x<t>, each shaped n_x by m
description: Sets the time-step notation and batch shape used by the RNN, GRU, LSTM, and seq2seq formulas.

input: sequence of token or feature vectors
shape.explanation: Each time step keeps feature width by batch columns; recurrence moves along t.

title: Vanilla RNN Hidden State
plainTextFormula: a<t> = g(W_aa a<t-1> + W_ax x<t> + b_a)
description: Updates recurrent hidden state using previous memory and the current input.

symbols.meaning: Hidden state at time step t

shape.explanation: The recurrent core emits one hidden state per time step and batch example.

title: RNN Output Prediction
plainTextFormula: yhat<t> = g_y(W_ya a<t> + b_y)
description: Maps hidden state at a time step into an emitted output.

shape.explanation: The output layer converts recurrent state width into output width.

title: RNN Sequence Loss
plainTextFormula: sequence loss sums per-time-step losses over the output sequence
description: Aggregates the prediction loss across output time steps.

shape.explanation: Summing over time collapses the sequence into one training objective.

title: Backpropagation Through Time
plainTextFormula: BPTT sums parameter-gradient contributions across time steps
description: Backpropagation through time reuses the same recurrent parameters at every time step and sums their gradient contributions.

shape.output: gradient with same shape as W
shape.explanation: Because W is shared over time, its total gradient is the sum of all unrolled contributions.

title: GRU Gate Equations
latex: \Gamma_u=\sigma(W_u[c^{\langle t-1\rangle},x^{\langle t\rangle}]+b_u),\quad \Gamma_r=\sigma(W_r[c^{\langle t-1\rangle},x^{\langle t\rangle}]+b_r),\quad \tilde{c}^{\langle t\rangle}=\tanh(W_c[\Gamma_r*c^{\langle t-1\rangle},x^{\langle t\rangle}]+b_c),\quad c^{\langle t\rangle}=\Gamma_u*\tilde{c}^{\langle t\rangle}+(1-\Gamma_u)*c^{\langle t-1\rangle}
plainTextFormula: GRU update gate, reset gate, candidate memory, and new memory
description: Uses update and reset gates to control how much previous memory is kept and how much candidate memory is written.

shape.explanation: All gates and candidate memory share the hidden-state shape for elementwise interpolation.

title: LSTM Gate Equations
plainTextFormula: LSTM forget gate, input gate, output gate from previous hidden state and current input
description: Controls what memory to forget, write, and expose at each LSTM time step.

shape.explanation: Each gate has the same hidden-state shape so it can mask memory elementwise.

title: LSTM Cell and Hidden Update
latex: \tilde{c}^{\langle t\rangle}=\tanh(W_c[a^{\langle t-1\rangle},x^{\langle t\rangle}]+b_c),\quad c^{\langle t\rangle}=f_t*c^{\langle t-1\rangle}+i_t*\tilde{c}^{\langle t\rangle},\quad a^{\langle t\rangle}=o_t*\tanh(c^{\langle t\rangle})
plainTextFormula: LSTM candidate memory, cell update, and hidden output
description: Writes candidate memory into the cell state through the input gate, keeps old memory through the forget gate, and exposes hidden state through the output gate.

shape.output: cell and hidden state: n_a x m
shape.explanation: The gate masks and memory tensors must match for elementwise multiplication and addition.

title: Bidirectional RNN Context
latex: a^{\langle t\rangle}=[\overrightarrow{a}^{\langle t\rangle};\overleftarrow{a}^{\langle t\rangle}],\quad \hat{y}^{\langle t\rangle}=g_y(W_y a^{\langle t\rangle}+b_y)
plainTextFormula: bidirectional state concatenates forward and backward hidden states before prediction
description: Uses both past and future sequence context by concatenating forward and backward recurrent states.

shape.explanation: Concatenation doubles the recurrent feature width before the output layer.

title: Q/K/V Projections
plainTextFormula: Q = X W_Q, K = X W_K, V = X W_V
description: Projects token representations into query, key, and value spaces.

shape.explanation: Projection matrices change representation width while preserving sequence positions.

title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
plainTextFormula: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V
description: Computes attention weights from query-key similarity, then mixes value vectors.

shape.explanation: QK^T creates scores over keys, and multiplying by V returns one value mixture per query.

title: Scaled Attention Shape Check
latex: Q\in\mathbb{R}^{T_q\times d_k},\quad K^T\in\mathbb{R}^{d_k\times T_k}\Rightarrow QK^T\in\mathbb{R}^{T_q\times T_k},\quad \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V\in\mathbb{R}^{T_q\times d_v}
plainTextFormula: Q shape T_q x d_k times K^T shape d_k x T_k gives scores T_q x T_k; scores times V gives T_q x d_v
description: Checks the matrix shapes inside scaled dot-product attention.

shape.explanation: The attention-weight matrix maps each query to a distribution over key/value positions.

title: Multi-Head Attention
plainTextFormula: MHA(Q,K,V) = Concat(head_1,...,head_h) W_O
description: Runs several attention heads in parallel and projects their concatenated outputs.

shape.explanation: Heads are concatenated along feature width and projected back to model width.

title: Transformer Block Pipeline
plainTextFormula: Transformer block pipeline: MHA, AddNorm, FFN, AddNorm
description: High-level formula flow of a Transformer block.

shape.explanation: Residual and normalization steps preserve model width.

title: Train / Validation / Test Roles
plainTextFormula: Train, validation, and test are distinct roles
description: Training fits parameters, validation tunes decisions, and test estimates final generalization.

shape.explanation: The important constraint is separation of roles, not a matrix operation.

title: Repeated Test Peeking Bias
plainTextFormula: Repeated test peeking biases the final test score
description: Using the test set repeatedly turns it into a model-selection signal.

shape.explanation: This is an evaluation protocol warning.

title: Confusion Matrix Counts
plainTextFormula: true positives, false positives, true negatives, false negatives
description: Four counts that summarize binary classification outcomes.

shape.explanation: Counts are accumulated across examples.

title: Precision / Recall / F1
plainTextFormula: precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), F1 = 2PR/(P+R)
description: Metrics for evaluating positive-class quality beyond accuracy.

symbols.meaning: Harmonic mean of precision and recall

shape.explanation: Each metric summarizes classification behavior across examples.

title: Bias / Variance Gap Labels
plainTextFormula: training error gap indicates bias, dev-train gap indicates variance
description: Uses error gaps to decide whether a model has bias, variance, or mismatch problems.

shape.explanation: Differences between scalar error rates guide next experiments.

title: Data Mismatch Gap
plainTextFormula: dev error minus train-dev error indicates data mismatch
description: Separates ordinary variance from distribution mismatch between training and development data.

symbols.meaning: Error on held-out data from the training distribution

shape.explanation: A larger dev gap suggests the dev distribution differs from training data.

title: Transfer Learning New Head
plainTextFormula: yhat = g_new(h_pretrained(x))
description: Uses a pretrained feature extractor and a new task-specific prediction head.

shape.explanation: The backbone maps input into features; the new head maps features to the new label space.

title: Frozen and Trainable Parameters
plainTextFormula: theta = [theta_frozen, theta_trainable]
description: Separates reused pretrained parameters from parameters updated for the target task.

shape.explanation: This is a parameter partition rather than a tensor multiplication.

title: BatchNorm Mini-batch Statistics
plainTextFormula: mu_B[l] = 1/m sum_i z[l](i), sigma_B2[l] = 1/m sum_i (z[l](i) - mu_B[l]) elementwise squared
description: Computes the mini-batch mean and variance for dense-layer pre-activations.

shape.explanation: BatchNorm reduces the batch axis while keeping one statistic per layer unit.

title: BatchNorm Single-example Normalize
plainTextFormula: zhat[l](i) = (z[l](i) - mu_B[l]) / sqrt(sigma_B2[l] + epsilon)
description: Normalizes one pre-activation column with the current mini-batch statistics.

shape.explanation: Subtraction, square root, and division are elementwise across the layer-unit axis.

title: BatchNorm Vectorized Normalize
plainTextFormula: Zhat[l] = (Z[l] - mu_B[l]) / sqrt(sigma_B2[l] + epsilon)
description: Normalizes the whole pre-activation matrix by broadcasting the mini-batch statistics across examples.

shape.explanation: The n[l] x 1 statistics broadcast across the m examples.

title: BatchNorm Normalize, Scale, and Shift
plainTextFormula: Ztilde[l] = gamma[l] * Zhat[l] + beta[l]
description: Applies the learned scale and shift after vectorized normalization.

shape.explanation: Gamma and beta broadcast across the m examples.

title: BatchNorm Single and Vectorized Scale-Shift
plainTextFormula: ztilde[l](i) = gamma[l] * zhat[l](i) + beta[l], Ztilde[l] = gamma[l] * Zhat[l] + beta[l]
description: Shows the single-example and vectorized learned affine transform after normalization.

shape.explanation: The learned parameters keep one scale and shift per layer unit, then broadcast across examples.

title: Dense-layer BatchNorm Forward Pipeline
plainTextFormula: Z[l] -> mu_B[l], sigma_B2[l] -> Zhat[l] -> Ztilde[l] -> A[l] = g[l](Ztilde[l])
description: Summarizes the dense-layer BatchNorm forward pass from pre-activations to the post-activation output.

shape.explanation: Each BatchNorm stage preserves the layer-by-batch matrix shape before activation.

title: BatchNorm Running Mean and Variance
plainTextFormula: mu_run[l] <- rho mu_run[l] + (1-rho) mu_B[l], sigma_run2[l] <- rho sigma_run2[l] + (1-rho) sigma_B2[l]
description: Maintains population-style running estimates used when the model is evaluated or deployed.

shape.explanation: The moving averages keep the same per-unit statistic shape.

title: BatchNorm Training Normalization
plainTextFormula: Zhat_train[l] = (Z[l] - mu_B[l]) / sqrt(sigma_B2[l] + epsilon)
description: Uses current mini-batch statistics during training mode.

shape.explanation: Training mode depends on the current mini-batch.

title: BatchNorm Training Scale and Shift
plainTextFormula: Ztilde_train[l] = gamma[l] * Zhat_train[l] + beta[l]
description: Applies learned gamma and beta to the training-mode normalized activations.

shape.explanation: Gamma and beta broadcast across the training examples.

title: BatchNorm Inference Normalization
plainTextFormula: Zhat_test[l] = (Z[l] - mu_run[l]) / sqrt(sigma_run2[l] + epsilon)
description: Uses running statistics at inference time so predictions do not depend on other examples in the current batch.

shape.explanation: Running statistics broadcast across inference examples.

title: BatchNorm Inference Transform
plainTextFormula: Ztilde_test[l] = gamma[l] * Zhat_test[l] + beta[l]
description: Applies learned gamma and beta after inference-mode normalization with running statistics.

shape.explanation: Inference uses fixed statistics, then the same learned affine parameters as training.

title: BatchNorm Parameter and Statistic Shapes
plainTextFormula: Z, Zhat, Ztilde shapes n[l] x m; batch stats, gamma, beta, running stats shapes n[l] x 1
description: Collects the core BatchNorm matrix and column-vector shapes for dense-layer notation.

shape.explanation: BatchNorm normalizes each layer unit across the batch, so statistics and learned parameters are column vectors.

title: VGG-style Convolution Block
plainTextFormula: VGG block repeats 3x3 conv + ReLU, then applies 2x2 max pooling
description: Represents the VGG-style habit of stacking small 3x3 convolutions before pooling.

shape.explanation: The convolutions learn features; the pooling step usually reduces spatial resolution.

title: Inception Channel Concatenation
plainTextFormula: Inception output concatenates 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, and pooling branch outputs along channels
description: Combines parallel convolution and pooling branches by concatenating their feature maps along the channel axis.

symbols.shape: same H and W, different channel counts

input: branch outputs with matching spatial size
shape.output: one feature tensor with summed channels
shape.explanation: Inception needs branch spatial sizes to match; channel counts are stacked.

title: Bottleneck Parameter Reduction
plainTextFormula: bottleneck params = C_in*C_mid + k^2*C_mid*C_out with C_mid much smaller than input/output channels
description: Uses a 1x1 projection to reduce channel width before an expensive spatial convolution.

shape.explanation: Reducing channels before the k by k convolution lowers the dominant parameter term.

title: Residual Block Forward Pass
plainTextFormula: y = F(x, W_i) + x
description: Adds a learned residual correction to the shortcut input, making very deep networks easier to optimize.

symbols.meaning: Shortcut input to the residual block
symbols.shape: same as F(x) for identity shortcuts

shape.explanation: The addition is valid only when the shortcut and residual branch have matching shapes.

title: Residual Projection Shortcut
plainTextFormula: y = F(x, W_i) + W_s x
description: Uses a learned projection on the shortcut path when the residual branch changes width or spatial resolution.

shape.explanation: Projection makes the shortcut compatible with the residual branch before addition.

title: YOLO Box Representation
plainTextFormula: a YOLO prediction stores box center x,y, width, height, objectness p_c, and class scores
description: Collects the per-box quantities predicted by a YOLO-style detection head.

symbols.meaning: Objectness or confidence that an object exists

shape.explanation: The 5 terms are x, y, w, h, and objectness; class terms add C more values.

title: YOLO Grid Output Shape
plainTextFormula: Y has shape S x S x (B*5 + C)
description: Classic YOLO predicts B boxes and C class scores for each grid cell.
aliases: S x S x B times 5 plus C

symbols.meaning: Number of predicted boxes per cell

input: image divided into S \times S cells
shape.explanation: Each box contributes x, y, w, h, confidence; class scores are stored per cell in the classic formulation.

title: YOLO Anchor Box Parameterization
plainTextFormula: b_x = sigmoid(t_x)+c_x, b_y = sigmoid(t_y)+c_y, b_w = p_w exp(t_w), b_h = p_h exp(t_h)
description: Converts network outputs into an anchor-relative bounding box in many YOLO-style detectors.

symbols.meaning: Raw box outputs from the model

shape.explanation: Sigmoid keeps the center near the cell while exponentials scale the anchor size.

title: YOLO Anchor Assignment
plainTextFormula: assign an object to the anchor whose shape has the highest IoU with the ground-truth box
description: Chooses the anchor box responsible for predicting an object by matching anchor shape to the ground-truth box.

shape.explanation: Anchor assignment is a matching rule that decides which predictor owns an object.

title: Intersection over Union
plainTextFormula: IoU(A,B) = area of intersection / area of union
description: Measures overlap between two bounding boxes, usually a prediction and ground truth.

shape.explanation: IoU is 1 for perfect overlap and 0 for no overlap.

title: Non-Max Suppression Rule
plainTextFormula: keep box i if IoU(box_i, best_box) is below threshold tau
description: Suppresses duplicate detections that overlap too much with a higher-confidence box.

shape.explanation: NMS is an algorithmic selection rule, not a differentiable layer.

title: Face Verification Distance
plainTextFormula: distance = L2 norm between two face embeddings
description: Compares two face embeddings; smaller distance means the faces are more likely to match.

symbols.meaning: Embedding produced by the face network

shape.explanation: The vector difference is collapsed to one distance value.

title: Triplet Loss
description: Trains embeddings so an anchor is closer to a positive example than to a negative example by a margin.

symbols.meaning: Positive example of the same identity
Negative example of a different identity

input: three embeddings of the same dimension
shape.explanation: Two squared distances and a margin are combined into one nonnegative loss.

title: Neural Style Content Cost
plainTextFormula: content cost = 1/2 Frobenius norm between content and generated activations
description: Keeps the generated image close to the content image in a chosen hidden layer.

shape.explanation: The Frobenius norm sums differences across spatial positions and channels.

title: Neural Style Gram Matrix
plainTextFormula: Gram matrix entry equals sum over spatial positions of channel i times channel j
description: Measures how strongly feature channels co-activate, which captures texture-like style information.

shape.explanation: The spatial axes are summed out, leaving channel-by-channel correlations.

title: Neural Style Cost
plainTextFormula: style cost compares style and generated Gram matrices
description: Matches channel-correlation statistics between the style image and generated image.

shape.explanation: The cost averages squared differences over all channel pairs.

title: Neural Style Transfer Total Cost
plainTextFormula: total neural style cost = alpha content cost + beta style cost
description: Balances content preservation and style matching while optimizing the generated image.

shape.explanation: The content and style losses are scalar terms combined by user-chosen weights.

title: Embedding Lookup
plainTextFormula: embedding vector e_t = E^T one-hot token o_t
description: Converts a one-hot token into a dense embedding vector by selecting a row of the embedding table.

shape.explanation: Multiplication by a one-hot vector selects the token embedding.

title: Cosine Similarity
plainTextFormula: cosine similarity = dot product divided by product of vector norms
description: Compares vector direction, often used for word or image embeddings.

shape.explanation: The dot product and norms reduce the vectors to one similarity score.

title: Skip-gram Softmax Probability
plainTextFormula: P(context word c | center word w) = exp(u_c^T v_w) / sum_j exp(u_j^T v_w)
description: Predicts a context word from a center-word embedding in the skip-gram objective.

symbols.meaning: Output embedding for context word c

shape.explanation: The denominator normalizes scores across every vocabulary item.

title: Negative Sampling Loss
plainTextFormula: negative sampling loss = positive logistic loss plus K negative logistic losses
description: Approximates the full softmax objective by contrasting one observed context word with sampled negative words.

symbols.meaning: Output vector for the observed context word
Output vector for sampled negative word k

shape.explanation: Each logistic term is scalar and the sampled terms are summed.

title: Seq2Seq Decoder Probability
plainTextFormula: P(y_t | previous output tokens, input x) = softmax(W_s s_t + b_s)
description: Maps the decoder state into a probability distribution for the next output token.

symbols.meaning: Decoder hidden state at step t

shape.explanation: Softmax produces one distribution over target tokens for each example.

title: Additive Attention Alignment Scores
plainTextFormula: alignment score e_t,s is transformed decoder state plus encoder state; alpha_t,s is softmax over source positions
description: Computes how much decoder step t should attend to encoder state s in additive seq2seq attention.

symbols.meaning: Unnormalized alignment score for decoder step t and source step s
Encoder hidden state at source position s

shape.output: attention weights over T_x source positions
shape.explanation: Scores are normalized over source positions so the weights for a decoder step sum to one.

title: Attention Context Vector
plainTextFormula: context vector c_t = sum_s attention weight alpha_t,s times encoder hidden state h_s
description: Builds a decoder-side context vector as a weighted mixture of encoder hidden states.

symbols.meaning: Context vector for decoder step t
Attention weight on source step s
Encoder hidden state at source step s

shape.explanation: The weighted sum preserves the encoder hidden-state width.

title: Beam Search Log Score
plainTextFormula: beam search score = sum over time of log next-token probabilities
description: Scores a candidate output sequence by accumulating log probabilities across decoding steps.

symbols.meaning: Output token at decoding step t

shape.explanation: Log probabilities are summed to avoid multiplying many small probabilities.

title: Length-Normalized Beam Score
plainTextFormula: normalized beam score = log probability sum divided by output length to alpha
description: Reduces beam search's tendency to prefer shorter sequences by normalizing the accumulated log score.

shape.explanation: The denominator adjusts the score without changing the candidate sequence itself.

title: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding
plainTextFormula: Transformer sinusoidal positional encoding with sine on even channels and cosine on odd channels
description: Adds deterministic position information to token embeddings before self-attention.

shape.explanation: Each token position receives one vector with the same width as the token embedding.

title: Layer Normalization
plainTextFormula: LayerNorm(x) = gamma * (x - mean) / sqrt(variance + epsilon) + beta
description: Normalizes across the feature dimension of each token independently, which works well for sequence models.

symbols.meaning: Mean and variance across features for one token

shape.explanation: LayerNorm preserves token count and model width.

title: Transformer Add & Norm
plainTextFormula: Add and Norm = LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))
description: Original Transformer post-norm form: add the residual connection, then normalize.

shape.explanation: Residual addition requires matching model-width tensors.

title: Transformer Feed-Forward Network
plainTextFormula: FFN(x) = ReLU(x W1 + b1) W2 + b2
description: Applies the same two-layer MLP independently to each token position.

symbols.meaning: Hidden width of the feed-forward network

shape.explanation: The FFN changes width internally but returns to model width.

title: Masked Self-Attention
plainTextFormula: masked attention = softmax((QK^T + mask) / sqrt(d_k)) V
description: Blocks attention to future tokens by adding a large negative mask before softmax.

symbols.meaning: Mask with 0 for allowed positions and negative infinity for blocked positions

shape.explanation: The mask has the same score-matrix shape as QK^T.

title: Matrix Multiplication Shape
plainTextFormula: A shape a x b times B shape b x c gives AB shape a x c
description: The inner dimensions must match; the outer dimensions become the result shape.
aliases: a x b times b x c

shape.explanation: The shared b dimension is summed over.

title: Dense Bias Broadcasting Shape
plainTextFormula: bias b shape n[l] x 1 broadcasts across m examples in Z = W A + b
description: Explains why one bias column can be added to every example in a dense layer batch.

shape.explanation: The bias column is reused for every example column in the batch.

title: Dense Layer Parameter Count
plainTextFormula: dense layer params = n[l] * n[l-1] weights plus n[l] biases
description: Counts all weights and biases in a fully connected layer.

shape.explanation: Weights contribute n[l] times n[l-1] parameters and biases contribute n[l] more.
